topic: Nango vs Composio vs Arcade Agent Auth 2026
keyword: Nango vs Composio vs Arcade agent auth

competitors.title: Merge.dev vs Nango: Which API integration platform should you choose in 2026?
key_points: Nango is an agentic API integrations platform where coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) write integrations as code
800+ APIs across 30 categories on a single runtime covering auth, tool calls, data syncs, webhooks, and MCP
Open source with self-hosting available; white-label auth is default (not Enterprise-gated)
SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, and HIPAA compliant; per-customer configuration in code
Pricing: usage-based (connections $1/mo, proxy requests $0.0001/req, functions compute $0.0000002/ms)

competitors.title: Best Composio Alternatives for Production AI Agents (Arcade Blog, June 2026)
key_points: Arcade is the MCP runtime for production AI agents — unifies auth, tools, and governance in one execution layer
8,000+ agent-optimized MCP tools with constrained schemas reducing hallucination surface area
Delegated per-user authorization with just-in-time permissions; tokens vaulted away from LLM context
Raised $60M Series A (June 2026) led by SYN Ventures with Morgan Stanley and Wipro
Built by team from Okta, Snowflake, Redis, Airbyte, MongoDB; authored MCP tool authorization spec
SOC 2 Type 2 certified; immutable OpenTelemetry-compatible audit logs; pre/post-tool-call hooks
Deployment: cloud, VPC, on-prem, or air-gapped

competitors.title: Composio — For AI agents: signup without a human
key_points: 1,000+ toolkits and 20,000+ tools through MCP and direct APIs — broadest integration catalog
Agent-native signup: AI agents can create their own Composio identity without human intervention
Features: smart tool search by intent, per-user auth, triggers/webhooks, workbench sandbox, CLI, MCP Gateway
May 2026 security incident: attacker accessed internal systems, exposed ~0.3% of active connections including 5,001 GitHub tokens
Responded with credential rotation across ~100 toolkits; introducing customer-key self-custody (Zero Trust Proxy KMS)
Best for rapid prototyping and single-user internal utilities; architectural limitations around multi-user auth and governance

competitors.title: Arcade: The MCP Runtime for Production AI Agents
key_points: Solves three problems: agent authorization (per-user dynamic permissions), tool reliability (intent-level tools not raw API wrappers), governance (audit logs for every action)
Framework agnostic: works with LangChain, LlamaIndex, Mastra, CrewAI, Pydantic, Google ADK, OpenAI Agents
Customers include LangChain, Snyk, Relevance AI, Sybill
MCP runtime handles auth, tool execution, and policy enforcement in one layer

competitors.title: Nango — Build integrations with AI
key_points: Integrations as code: coding agents write, test, and deploy integrations against real connections
Covers API auth, tool calls, data syncs, webhooks, polling triggers, and custom unified APIs on one platform
1M+ integrations running in production; 99.9% uptime; used by hundreds of SaaS and AI companies
Open source (GitHub); self-hosting available on Enterprise plan
